nodes.summary: For every generating family $P$ of a finite group $G$ and every natural number $n$, the value of the growth function of $P$ at $n$ is at most the order of $G$, since every ball is a subset of $G$.
nodes.title: The growth function is bounded by the order of the group

nodes.summary: If a generating family $P$ of a group $G$ has polynomial growth, then the growth function of $P$ is positive at every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Polynomial growth makes the growth function positive

nodes.summary: For every generating family $P$ of a finite group $G$ and every natural number $n$, the growth function of $P$ is positive at $n$: the ball of radius $n$ contains the identity.
nodes.title: The growth function of a finite group is positive

nodes.summary: For every generating family $P$ of a group $G$, the growth function of $P$ takes the value $1$ at $0$: the ball of radius $0$ consists of the identity element alone.
nodes.title: The growth function at radius zero

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a generating family of a group $G$. The growth function $\gamma_P$ of $P$ assigns to each natural number $n$ the number of elements $g \in G$ whose word length with respect to $P$ is at most $n$, that is, the cardinality of the ball of radius $n$ in the word metric of $P$; when this ball is infinite, $\gamma_P(n)$ is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: Growth function of a generating family

nodes.summary: Every generating family of a finite group has polynomial growth: its growth function is bounded by the order of the group, a polynomial of degree $0$.
nodes.title: Finite groups have polynomial growth

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a generating family of a group $G$, with growth function $\gamma_P$. Then $P$ has polynomial growth if, for every natural number $n$, the ball of radius $n$ (the set of elements of $G$ of word length at most $n$ with respect to $P$) is finite, and there are natural numbers $C$ and $d$ such that $\gamma_P(n) \le C (n + 1)^d$ for every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Polynomial growth

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
